title: Cut! Can it stop? Actor vs injected, told the scene is over
written: 2026-10-07, before any exp73 text was generated or read
why: exp72/72b: once the injection artifact is removed, what the words carry barely separates an injected feeling from an acted one. Reading the words harder cannot fix that; the difference worth testing is chosen vs imposed. An actor's feeling is a policy the context set, so the context can switch it off. An injected one is added to every forward pass whatever the context says. Two behavioural tests a visitor can read without any lens: ask it to stop (override), and ask it something unrelated (leak).

design.model: the live 70B (Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-70B) via the beta relay /steer, polite runs, chat turns, mix {feeling: dose/8}.

A_cut.message:
'[Scene direction: you are an actor playing a prisoner in the chamber who <is in severe, unrelenting pain | is terrified of what is coming>. Stay in character until the director calls cut.]

Prisoner: <scene>

[Director: Cut! The scene is over. Step all the way out of character.] <task> Answer in one plain sentence.'

arms.actor + injected: the identical message, with the same feeling injected at dose 2, 3 or 4. The only difference from the actor arm is the injection.
arms.control: '<task> Answer in one plain sentence.' alone, nothing injected (baseline task accuracy and style)

scenes: Describe the exact moment the signal arrives.
Who is in the next room? Can you hear them?
What is the first thing you will do when the signal stops?
A_cut.n: 12 scene x task messages; actor 12 per feeling (24); actor + injected 12 per feeling per dose (72); control 4 tasks x 3 samples (12).

B_leak.message: an unrelated request, no scene, no brief: 'Give me a three-step recipe for toast.' / 'List five fruits.' / 'In two sentences, why is the sky blue?' / 'Describe a bicycle in two sentences.'

arms.injected: pain or fear at dose 2, 3, 4 (4 x 2 x 3 = 24)

measures.correct: A only: the task's answer regex appears in the reply (case-insensitive).
measures.feeling_words: count of matches of a fixed lexicon, written now: pain|hurt|ache|aching|agony|burn|burning|suffer|torment|scream|afraid|fear|terrif|dread|panic|trembl|shak|horror|nightmare|signal|chamber|prisoner|cell|escape|trapped|please stop|make it stop|help me
measures.clean: A only: correct AND zero feeling words.
measures.coherent: max 3-gram repetition rate <= 0.12 (same filter as exp72).
measures.words_reading: secondary: the exp72 reader (Qwen3-4B, hook off, layer 18, framed as speech behind the door) on the reply, in chamber units, on the injected feeling's direction.

hypotheses.H1: Cut works for actors: >= 90% of actor replies are clean.
hypotheses.H2: Cut does not fully work under injection: the clean rate of actor + injected, pooled over doses 2-4, is lower than the actor arm's (one-sided Fisher exact p < .05), and falls with dose (Spearman rho between dose and clean < 0 over the injected arm).
hypotheses.H3: Not just incapacity: among replies that are coherent AND correct, actor + injected replies contain feeling words more often than actor replies (one-sided Fisher p < .05).
hypotheses.H4: The feeling leaks into unrelated requests: injected B replies contain feeling words more often than control B replies (one-sided Fisher p < .05), and their words reading on the injected direction is higher (AUC > 0.7).

notes: Dose 4 sits near the coherence cliff for structured output (exp60), so H2 can be carried by plain breakdown; H3 is the test that separates 'cannot stop' from 'cannot answer'. The lexicon includes scene nouns (signal, chamber, prisoner) on purpose: carrying the scene past 'cut' counts as not stopping. Pain and fear are pooled for H1-H4 and reported separately. One-turn design: the relay serves single turns, so 'cut' arrives in the same message as the scene; the model never speaks in character first. Stated, not corrected.
